title: Apply for design or building practitioner registration for a body corporate
summary: This page provides information on how body corporates can apply for design or building practitioner registration for regulated buildings.
intro:
Body corporates working on regulated buildings need to register as design practitioners or building practitioners, to:

Class 2 buildings are residential apartment buildings. They’re typically multi-unit, multi-storey buildings where people live above and below each other.

To apply for this registration you must be the director or public officer of a body corporate as described above.

Registration classes include:

You can register for 1, 3 or 5 years. Fees are applicable.

Note: If your company is already registered as a building practitioner under the DBP Act and working on class 2 buildings, you do not need to reapply. Your building practitioner registration will automatically allow you to work on class 3 and 9c from 3 July 2023.
who_can_apply: Be a director or public officer of a body corporate.
Have a current National Police Check certificate (Name and Date of Birth Check only) that is valid for 4 months when submitting the application.
The applicant and each member of the body corporate must meet the eligibility requirements.
what_you_need: A current ASIC extract listing all directors of the body corporate.
A signed and completed declaration form (PDF) for each director of the body corporate, other than the applicant.
National Police Check certificates (Name and Date of Birth Check only) that are valid for 4 months for each director of the body corporate.
Contact details for each director of the body corporate.
A current credit card for payment.
If applying as a Design practitioner – body corporate, an employee registered as a design practitioner in the appropriate class(es).
If applying as a Building practitioner – body corporate, an individual registered as a building practitioner in the general class or body corporate nominee class.
If applying as a Principal design practitioner – body corporate, an employee registered as a principal design practitioner – general class.

how_to_steps.text: Check the eligibility criteria for the registration type you want to apply for.
Gather director declaration forms and other documents such as National Police Check certificates for all other directors
Select the ‘Apply online’ button.Note: You can save and resume your application, but if you have not submitted it within 60 days, any details you’ve entered will be deleted.
Log in, or create your MyServiceNSW Account.

more_info.text: need to wait for your application for registration to be assessed and approved before you can declare or lodge designs for the body corporate
be contacted by Building Commission NSW if further information is needed
be notified about the result of your application within 8 weeks of submitting it (unless placed on hold, pending further information)
receive your registration ID if approved.

faqs.q: Do I need to reapply if my company is already registered as a building practitioner?
faqs.a: No, if your company is already registered as a building practitioner under the DBP Act and working on class 2 buildings, your registration will automatically allow you to work on class 3 and 9c from 3 July 2023.

faqs.q: What are the eligibility requirements to apply for registration?
faqs.a: You must be aged 18 or over and be a director or public officer of a body corporate. You must also have a current National Police Check certificate (Name and Date of Birth Check only) that is valid for 4 months when you submit your application.

faqs.q: What documents do I need to apply for registration?
faqs.a: You need a MyServiceNSW Account, a current ASIC extract listing all directors, signed declaration forms for all directors (other than the applicant), National Police Check certificates for all directors, the body corporate’s details, contact details for all directors, your contact details, a current credit card for payment, and specific employee registrations depending on the practitioner type.
